dial.summary: 4/8 indicators supportive on November 15 — BTC.D firm at ~59.3% and perp funding rates declining further to 0.0028% (near-zero, ~3% annualized) signal continued deleveraging without systemic stress; ISM Manufacturing holding at 55.5 (10th consecutive expansion) and Global M2 at $104.3T sustain the macro bid; DXY at 103.28 (headwind, above 100 threshold) and real yields at 2.86% (flat on 4-week basis, neutral) remain primary headwinds; next key catalysts are the Nov 25 Oct PCE print and the December 9 FOMC decision.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: MacroMicro G4 aggregate (US/Euro Zone/China/Japan) at ~$104.3T as of September 2026 (104,317.08B per MacroMicro series); October G4 data not yet published as of November 15, 2026 — typically updated mid-to-late November following the reference month; broader global M2 estimate from StreetStats cited by Au79 Macro (Nov 14): $103.89T, with Bitrue citing $103.66T — these are wider aggregates than the G4 series; US M2 $23.41T in Sep 2026 (+5.7% YoY per FRED H.6, next release Nov 24); 4-week Aug→Sep G4 change: +$0.64T (+0.6%), above flat threshold — trend UP; status supportive (4-week G4 trend up, no YoY contraction); held unchanged pending October G4 publication.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: October 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI at 55.5% (released November 2, 2026), beating consensus 54.7%, up 1.0pp from September's 54.5%; 10th consecutive expansion month; Production sub-index 59.0 (highest since Nov 2021), New Orders 55.5, Employment 52.4; Prices Paid fell to 75.2 from September's 77.9, though input price pressures remain elevated; 4-week trend UP (Sep 54.5 → Oct 55.5, +1.0pp); status supportive (above 50 and rising); next ISM Manufacturing release December 1, 2026 (November data); value unchanged — October 55.5 is the current monthly reading.

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY spot 103.28 as of Friday November 13, 2026 close (GuruFocus: 103.278; CNBC: 103.411 intraday high, 52-week high set Nov 13); no new data Nov 14–15 (weekend); 4-week trend UP — from ~101.5–101.8 on October 14 to 103.28 on November 13, net +~1.5–1.8%, well above the 0.5% flat threshold; hot October CPI (+0.4% MoM, Nov 10 release) and hawkish Fed repricing drove the DXY push; Fed Chair Warsh speech scheduled November 16 is next key catalyst; status headwind (DXY above 100 — must fall below 97.5 for supportive); FRED DTWEXBGS network-restricted — ICE spot corroborated via GuruFocus and CNBC.

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: 10-year TIPS real yield (DFII10) at 2.86% on November 12, 2026 (FRED series; next scheduled release Nov 16, 2026); recent readings: Nov 6: 2.63%, Nov 9: 2.66%, Nov 10: 2.78%, Nov 12: 2.86%; 4-week trend FLAT — from approximately 2.85–2.90% on October 14 (Oct 5 high 2.95%) to 2.86% on November 12, net change ~0 to -4bps within flat threshold; status neutral (above 2% but flat trend — headwind requires BOTH rising trend AND above 2%; neither fully met); 10Y nominal 5.14–5.15% per Nov 13 Forbes data, 2Y 4.86–4.88%; next DFII10 release Nov 16 will reflect Nov 13-14 market moves; 52-week range 1.72%–2.95%.

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: 2s10s spread at approximately +27bps as of Friday November 13, 2026 close (Forbes Nov 13: 10Y 5.15%, 2Y 4.88%, spread 27bps; weekly recap: spread 0.28% end of week; yieldcurve.pro Nov 10: +25bps); 4-week trend FLAT — from approximately +28–32bps on October 14 to +27bps on November 13, net change approximately -1 to -5bps within flat threshold; 10Y rose ~30bps over the week as hot CPI repriced December FOMC hike odds; 2Y also spiked (worst week since 2024, +35–42bps), keeping spread roughly stable; status neutral (positive spread, no sustained steepening, not deeply inverted — headwind requires < -50bps which is far away); next inflection: December 9 FOMC decision impact on 2Y repricing.

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: $6,758,867M ($6.759T) for week ended November 11, 2026 (H.4.1 released November 12, 2026; +$10,722M WoW from Nov 4's $6,748,145M, +$178,405M YoY); prior weekly readings: Nov 4 $6,748,145M, Oct 28 $6,745,635M, Oct 21 $6,753,604M, Oct 14 $6,755,639M; 4-week change Oct 14 → Nov 11: +$3,228M (~+$3.2B, essentially flat); Fed net liquidity (WALCL minus TGA minus ON RRP) at ~$5,846.58B per Nov 14 Au79 market note; balance sheet stabilized post-QT-pause (QT ended December 2025); YoY +$178.4B (+2.7%); status supportive (flat with slight growth, no aggressive QT); next H.4.1 release November 19 (covering week of November 18).

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: CoinGlass BTC perp funding rate 0.0028% per 8h (~3.0% annualized) as of November 15, 2026 (down from 0.0046–0.0052% on Nov 14); OI-weighted rate 0.0046% per CoinGlass Nov 14 snapshot; Au79 macro report (Nov 14): OI-weighted rate 0.0083% per 8h with BTC futures open interest at $51.06B; Brave New Coin (Nov 14): negative funding on Binance, OKX, and Bybit on Nov 13 (short traders paying longs); BTC at ~$67–69K with $700M+ liquidations in 24h (92% longs per CoinGlass Nov 13–14); 30-day trend FLAT — mid-October rates were near zero/slightly negative, now 0.0028%, within flat noise range; status supportive (well below 0.04% headwind threshold); near-zero/negative funding on major exchanges is a classic accumulation signal; continued deleveraging without systemic stress.

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap $284.852B as of November 14, 2026 (DefiLlama: USDT ~61.5% of total); BTC.D at ~59.3% per TV Hub/CryptoPotato, BTC at ~$67–69K; implied TOTAL crypto market cap ~$2.24–2.27T (BTC mktcap ~$1.33T / 0.593); implied stablecoin dominance ~12.5% ($284.852B / $2.26T); 30-day trend UP — October 14 dominance ~10.5–10.8%, November 15 ~12.5%, net +~1.7–2.0pp over 4 weeks; status neutral — headwind requires rising dominance AND rising TOTAL simultaneously; TOTAL has declined from ~$2.6T (Oct 14) to ~$2.26T (not rising), so headwind condition not met; supportive condition (falling 30-day dominance) also not met; rise in dominance reflects risk-off repositioning as BTC pullback from recent highs, but TOTAL contraction prevents headwind classification.

upcoming.title: US Retail Sales (October 2026)
upcoming.note: Census Bureau releases October 2026 Advance Monthly Retail Trade Survey at 8:30 AM ET; September retail sales were +0.8% MoM (well above the +0.3% forecast); a print above +0.5% MoM would add to the already-strong December 9 FOMC hike case after the hot October CPI (+0.4% MoM, released Nov 10) and October PPI (released Nov 13); DXY at 103.28 (52-week range top) reflects persistent inflation pressure; a miss near 0% would add soft-landing ambiguity but is unlikely to outweigh the inflation surprise given DXY elevated; this is among the last major growth reads before the ~November 29 FOMC blackout period ahead of the December 9 decision.

upcoming.title: Industrial Production (October 2026)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve releases October 2026 Industrial Production and Capacity Utilization (G.17) at 9:15 AM ET; September industrial production rose +0.4% MoM; a continued expansion would corroborate the October ISM Manufacturing PMI at 55.5 (10th consecutive expansion month); Fed plans an annual G.17 revision release on November 24, so this reading may be subject to revision; released same day as October Retail Sales.

upcoming.title: Housing Starts (October 2026)
upcoming.note: Census Bureau releases October 2026 New Residential Construction at 8:30 AM ET; elevated mortgage rates (30Y near 7.1%) and real yields at 2.86% (flat on 4-week basis but historically high) continue to pressure housing affordability; after the hot CPI print sealing higher-for-longer expectations, a sharp drop in permits would underscore the housing drag on Q4 2026 growth.

upcoming.title: FOMC Minutes — October 27–28 Meeting
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve releases minutes of the October 27–28 FOMC meeting at 2:00 PM ET; the Fed held at 3.75%–4.00% (vote 10–2) at that meeting; minutes will reveal member views on the threshold for a December 9 hike given elevated ISM Prices Paid and Iran-war supply shocks; both October CPI (+0.4% MoM, Nov 10) and October PPI (released Nov 13) arrived after the October meeting — markets will read the minutes against the new inflation reality; Fed Chair Warsh speech November 16 also sets tone ahead of these minutes; FOMC blackout period begins ~November 29 ahead of the December 9 decision.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended November 15, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL releases weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET on Thursday November 19; final weekly labor read before Thanksgiving and the ~November 29 FOMC blackout period; a sustained trend above 220K would pressure December 9 hike odds given the already-hot CPI (+0.4% MoM Oct) and elevated DXY (103.28); next NFP release is December 4 (November data), arriving just 5 days before the December 9 FOMC decision.

upcoming.title: Philadelphia Fed Manufacturing Index (November 2026)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia releases November 2026 Manufacturing Business Outlook Survey at 8:30 AM ET; provides a first-look at November manufacturing activity ahead of the December 1 ISM Manufacturing PMI; a positive print above 0 would reinforce the October ISM signal at 55.5 (10th consecutive expansion month); released on the third Thursday of the month, same day as jobless claims.

upcoming.title: Existing Home Sales (October 2026)
upcoming.note: National Association of Realtors releases October 2026 Existing Home Sales at 10:00 AM ET; mortgage rates near 7.1% continue to suppress turnover via the low-rate lock-in effect; provides a full-month housing transaction count for October; real yields holding at 2.86% (flat on 4-week basis) keep affordability severely constrained; watch for any inventory normalization trends.
